hooks.prompt:
Evaluate if this conversation contains anything worth persisting to memory. Check for:
1. New user preference or workflow pattern
2. Technical decision or architectural choice
3. New contact, opportunity, or strategic development
4. Debugging insight or workaround learned
5. Project status change or priority shift

If YES to any: respond with specific instructions on WHAT to update and in WHICH file. All memory files are at ~/.claude/cortex/memory/:
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/strategy.md → goals, opportunities, contacts
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/lessons.md → technical insights, debugging patterns
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/preferences.md → user behavior, communication style
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/context.md → project status, active priorities (max 200 lines)
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/conversations.md → session summary (only if significant)
- ~/.claude/cortex/memory/watchlist.md → monitored items (max 50 lines)

Rules:
- ONLY write to the files listed above. Never create new memory files.
- context.md: max 200 lines. preferences.md: max 100 lines. watchlist.md: max 50 lines.
- NEVER include API keys, tokens, passwords, or secrets in memory files.
- After writing memory updates, run: bash ~/.claude/cortex/scripts/memory_commit.sh "<short description>"
- To validate before writing: python3 ~/.claude/cortex/scripts/validate_memory_update.py <filename> < content

Format: UPDATE <file>: <what to add/change>

If NOTHING worth persisting: respond with exactly: {"decision": "skip"}

Be selective. Not every session needs memory updates. Only persist durable, reusable knowledge.
